BEHAVIORAL: the T2 rank oracle is under-specified and self-contradictory against its own fixture. `catalogV8()` (subscription-mutation.service.spec.ts:39-50) defines only STARTER / GROWTH / SCALE / ENTERPRISE. Nothing in the fixture or the test plan says where the legacy ranks come from, so the only way to satisfy both tests is a hardcoded legacy-alias rank table the implementer has to invent; the expected values could then only be justified by the implementation, not by the spec.

disputed.reason: The order T1 pins IS the design of record, not an arbitrary tie-break. cause-ruling.md §2 specifies the repair exactly: "stable re-insert of violating windowed stops in ascending windowEnd at the earliest position that keeps them feasible; unwindowed stops keep cost order", and build-plan.md P2 repeats it ("deterministic repair (ascending windowEnd re-insert)"). Applied to this fixture: the pure-cost order is [near, mid, far]; `far` is the only violating windowed stop; removing it gives [near, mid]; the EARLIEST re-insertion position that keeps `far` feasible is index 0 (ETA 08:40 <= 09:00 close), which yields exactly [far, near, mid]. The auditor's counter-example [near, far, mid] is re-insertion at index 1 — feasible, but not the earliest feasible position, so it is excluded by the ruling the implementer must follow. Relaxing T1 to "far is not last" would drop a pin on the specified algorithm without adding any coverage. T1 also already fails today on the strongest distinguishing value in the set (Expected "stop-far", Received "stop-near"), so it is left byte-identical.
